scope.goal: Preflight de compatibilidad de dispositivos para escritorio, laptop, tablet, Android e iPhone sin implementar cambios grandes.
inScope: estrategia de pruebas por viewport/dispositivo para las etapas posteriores

directedInspection.globalResponsiveBase: PASS__frontend/src/styles.scss uses min-width 320px, responsive media queries, bounded dialogs and horizontal table scrolling
directedInspection.applicationShell: PASS__frontend/src/app/app.component.scss has adaptive sidebar/topbar/content at 1180/1000/900/680/480px and safe-area-aware vertical layout
directedInspection.recentinventarioSurface: PASS__frontend/src/app/features/inventario/ajustes-list.component.ts includes responsive 1050/640px layouts and viewport-bounded modal behavior
directedInspection.testCapability: PASS__frontend/package.json exposes lint/build and Playwright E2E tooling

risks: Responsive CSS alone does not certify every workflow on physical Android/iPhone hardware.
Wide data tables may intentionally require horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.
Device-specific browser/keyboard/safe-area behavior must be exercised in N8.2.E/G rather than inferred in PRE.
acceptanceCriteria: No fixed desktop-only viewport contract blocks narrow devices.
Core application shell has explicit tablet/mobile behavior.
Critical overlays remain viewport bounded and usable at narrow widths.
Subsequent QA can exercise representative desktop, laptop, tablet, Android and iPhone viewport/device profiles without changing backend/domain contracts solely for device compatibility.
rollback: Evidence-only PRE stage: rollback is deletion/reversion of this review/receipt evidence; no runtime or schema mutation is introduced.

testStrategy.PRE: static directed inspection of viewport, shell, global responsive primitives and recent critical UI
testStrategy.FRONTEND_UX: apply only minimal responsive fixes if concrete defects are found
testStrategy.TEST_CI: lint/build plus targeted Playwright viewport/device coverage for desktop/laptop/tablet/Android/iPhone profiles; physical-device-only limitations must remain explicit rather than fabricated
